root_cause.text: F2FS created a per-superblock inline xattr slab cache in `f2fs_init_xattr_caches()` using a device-based name, but because the slab core can merge identical-sized caches and keep shared cache objects alive across mounts, destroying and recreating that per-sb cache caused a name collision and `kmem_cache_create()` warning on remount.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes `struct kmem_cache *inline_xattr_slab` and `inline_xattr_slab_size` from `struct f2fs_sb_info`, deletes per-mount `f2fs_init_xattr_caches()`/`f2fs_destroy_xattr_caches()` calls from `f2fs_fill_super()` and `f2fs_put_super()`, and replaces them with a single global `inline_xattr_slab` initialized once at fs init as `f2fs_kmem_cache_create("f2fs_xattr_entry", DEFAULT_XATTR_SLAB_SIZE)`, matching the report that two per-sb caches like `f2fs_xattr_entry-7:3` and `f2fs_xattr_entry-7:7` could share one underlying slab object and trigger “already exists” on recreation.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: F2FS created a per-superblock inline xattr slab cache in `f2fs_init_xattr_caches()` using a device-based name, but because the slab core can merge identical-sized caches and keep shared cache objects alive across mounts, destroying and recreating that per-sb cache caused a name collision and `kmem_cache_create()` warning on remount.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove inline xattr slab cache state from f2fs_sb_info as part of a structure cleanup.
intent_record.what: Two fields were removed from struct f2fs_sb_info: a struct kmem_cache pointer named inline_xattr_slab and an unsigned int named inline_xattr_slab_size, along with their associated comments.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the f2fs superblock info structure no longer stores per-filesystem state for an inline xattr slab cache or its default slab size, meaning any code using these members must no longer rely on them being present in this struct.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the xattr cache teardown call from f2fs_put_super during superblock cleanup.
intent_record.what: The call to `f2fs_destroy_xattr_caches(sbi);` was removed from `f2fs_put_super(struct super_block *sb)`.
intent_record.how: At unmount/superblock teardown time, the xattr cache destruction routine is no longer invoked from this path, changing cleanup behavior for the F2FS superblock shutdown sequence.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove xattr cache initialization from f2fs superblock setup and simplify the associated error unwind path.
intent_record.what: In f2fs_fill_super(), the call to f2fs_init_xattr_caches(sbi) and its associated error-handling jump label were removed. The f2fs_init_page_array_cache(sbi) call now follows directly after the previous initialization step, and its failure path now jumps to free_percpu instead of free_xattr_cache.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the filesystem no longer initializes the xattr slab caches during superblock setup. If page array cache initialization fails, control now skips directly to the per-CPU cleanup path, which changes the teardown sequence and removes dependency on a separate xattr-cache cleanup step in this path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the xattr cache cleanup from the `f2fs_fill_super()` unwind path and simplify the error-handling labels.
intent_record.what: The diff removes the `free_xattr_cache:` label and the associated call to `f2fs_destroy_xattr_caches(sbi)` from the error-unwind path in `f2fs_fill_super()`, leaving the control flow to fall through from `free_page_array_cache` directly to `free_percpu`.
intent_record.how: On failure cleanup during superblock initialization, the xattr cache destruction is no longer performed at this unwind point. This changes the teardown sequence by skipping xattr cache cleanup in this specific error path, likely because that cleanup is handled elsewhere or was no longer needed here.

intent_record.intent_summary: Initialize the xattr cache before filesystem registration and clean it up on registration failure.
intent_record.what: In `init_f2fs_fs()`, the call to `register_filesystem(&f2fs_fs_type)` was moved later, after a new call to `f2fs_init_xattr_cache()`. A new error path label `free_xattr_cache` was added to destroy the xattr cache if filesystem registration fails.
intent_record.how: At runtime, F2FS now initializes its xattr cache before registering the filesystem, ensuring that all required caches are set up before the filesystem becomes available. If registration fails, the newly created xattr cache is cleaned up, preventing a resource leak and keeping initialization failure handling consistent.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add missing xattr cache cleanup during F2FS filesystem shutdown.
intent_record.what: In the f2fs filesystem exit path, a call to f2fs_destroy_xattr_cache() was inserted after unregister_filesystem(&f2fs_fs_type) and before the existing cleanup calls for casefold and compress caches.
intent_record.how: At module/filesystem unload time, the xattr cache is now explicitly released, preventing that cache from remaining allocated after F2FS teardown and aligning cleanup with the other cache destruction steps.

intent_record.intent_summary: Switch inline xattr allocation to use a global slab cache and default slab size constant.
intent_record.what: A new static global pointer `inline_xattr_slab` was added, and `xattr_alloc()` was changed to compare `size` against `DEFAULT_XATTR_SLAB_SIZE` instead of `sbi->inline_xattr_slab_size`, and to allocate from `inline_xattr_slab` instead of `sbi->inline_xattr_slab`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, inline xattr allocations now use a shared/global slab cache and a fixed default slab size rather than relying on the per-superblock slab cache and size field. This changes which cache is used when allocating inline xattr storage and makes the allocation decision depend on the default size constant.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix inline xattr freeing to use the correct slab cache reference.
intent_record.what: In `xattr_free()`, the `kmem_cache_free()` call for the inline xattr case was changed from using `sbi->inline_xattr_slab` to using `inline_xattr_slab` directly.
intent_record.how: At runtime, inline xattr memory will now be returned to the global/static `inline_xattr_slab` cache reference instead of dereferencing the superblock info object to get the slab pointer. This changes which slab allocator instance is used for freeing inline xattr objects and avoids relying on `sbi` for that path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Convert f2fs xattr cache management from per-superblock caches to a single global init-time cache.
intent_record.what: The functions were renamed and their scope changed from per-superblock cache management to a single global cache: `f2fs_init_xattr_caches(struct f2fs_sb_info *sbi)` became `f2fs_init_xattr_cache(void)` with `__init`, the device-specific slab name and per-sbi slab size calculation were removed, and it now creates `inline_xattr_slab` using the fixed name `"f2fs_xattr_entry"` and `DEFAULT_XATTR_SLAB_SIZE`. Similarly, `f2fs_destroy_xattr_caches(struct f2fs_sb_info *sbi)` became `f2fs_destroy_xattr_cache(void)` and destroys the global `inline_xattr_slab` instead of the per-sbi cache.
intent_record.how: At runtime, xattr cache setup/teardown is no longer tied to each mounted filesystem instance or block device. Instead, one shared xattr slab cache is initialized once during startup and destroyed once during shutdown, reducing per-superblock allocation logic and making cache lifetime global rather than mount-specific.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a derived default xattr slab size constant for consistent sizing calculations.
intent_record.what: A new macro, `DEFAULT_XATTR_SLAB_SIZE`, was added and defined as `DEFAULT_INLINE_XATTR_ADDRS * sizeof(__le32) + XATTR_PADDING_SIZE`.
intent_record.how: This introduces a reusable computed size constant for xattr slab allocation or sizing logic, allowing code elsewhere to use a standardized default slab size derived from the inline xattr address count plus padding.

intent_record.intent_summary: Refactor xattr cache initialization and destruction to init-time, argument-free helpers.
intent_record.what: The xattr cache function prototypes in the header were renamed and their signatures changed: f2fs_init_xattr_caches(struct f2fs_sb_info *) became int __init f2fs_init_xattr_cache(void), and f2fs_destroy_xattr_caches(struct f2fs_sb_info *) became void f2fs_destroy_xattr_cache(void).
intent_record.how: This changes the API so xattr cache initialization and teardown no longer take a superblock info argument, and initialization is marked as __init, indicating it is intended to run only during early setup and be discarded afterward. Runtime callers will use a global/init-time cache setup and cleanup path instead of per-superblock cache management.

intent_record.intent_summary: Rename and simplify the xattr cache stub helpers to use parameterless init/destroy interfaces with init-only annotation.
intent_record.what: The inline stub functions were renamed and had their signatures changed: `f2fs_init_xattr_caches(struct f2fs_sb_info *sbi)` became `f2fs_init_xattr_cache(void)`, and `f2fs_destroy_xattr_caches(struct f2fs_sb_info *sbi)` became `f2fs_destroy_xattr_cache(void)`. The init stub also gained the `__init` annotation.
intent_record.how: At runtime, these changes alter only the fallback no-op/no-op-like declarations used when the feature is not enabled. The init function no longer accepts an `sbi` argument, and the `__init` annotation marks it as initialization-only, allowing the kernel to treat it as init code. The destroy stub similarly no longer takes an argument, reflecting that no per-superblock cache object is being managed in this configuration.

grouping_result.intent: Rename and simplify the xattr cache stub helpers to use parameterless init/destroy interfaces with init-only annotation.
Remove the xattr cache teardown call from f2fs_put_super during superblock cleanup.
Convert f2fs xattr cache management from per-superblock caches to a single global init-time cache.
Remove the xattr cache cleanup from the `f2fs_fill_super()` unwind path and simplify the error-handling labels.
Add missing xattr cache cleanup during F2FS filesystem shutdown.
Switch inline xattr allocation to use a global slab cache and default slab size constant.
Fix inline xattr freeing to use the correct slab cache reference.
Add a derived default xattr slab size constant for consistent sizing calculations.

consistency_review.reason: Hunks 2 and 8 both focus on changing xattr cache management from per-superblock setup to a global cache and adjusting initialization/error handling, while Hunk 0 is specifically about removing inline slab cache state from f2fs_sb_info structure cleanup, which is a different structural goal.

consistency_review.core_intent: Clean up f2fs xattr slab cache handling and related structure/error-path cleanup in the superblock setup code.

consistency_review.core_intent: Ensure F2FS xattr cache lifecycle is correctly managed by initializing it before registration and cleaning it up on failure/shutdown.

relevance_review.reason: The changes are a refactor of xattr cache stub helper APIs to parameterless init/destroy interfaces, not a fix for the per-superblock slab cache name-collision/remount issue described in the root cause.

The root cause is a per-superblock xattr slab cache being destroyed and recreated across mounts, leading to cache name collisions on remount. Removing the xattr cache teardown from superblock cleanup directly addresses that lifecycle bug by preventing the cache from being destroyed before remount.

The changes directly address the root cause by removing per-superblock xattr cache creation and switching to a single global cache, which avoids the remount name-collision problem caused by recreating identical slab caches.

The root cause is tied to lifecycle handling of the per-superblock inline xattr slab cache. Removing xattr cache cleanup from the f2fs_fill_super() unwind path directly changes when that cache is destroyed, which is part of the remount/name-collision issue.

The fix adds missing xattr cache cleanup on F2FS shutdown, which directly relates to the root cause: per-superblock xattr slab caches were being destroyed/recreated across mounts, leading to cache name collisions on remount. Cleaning up the xattr cache is part of addressing that lifecycle issue.

The changes directly address the root cause by replacing the per-superblock inline xattr slab cache with a global slab cache and removing the per-sb cache state, which avoids the cache recreation/name-collision issue on remount.

The root cause is about incorrect handling of the per-superblock inline xattr slab cache across mounts. A fix to use the correct slab cache reference when freeing inline xattrs is directly related to managing that cache correctly and addresses the same area of failure.

This change only adds a derived default xattr slab size constant for sizing consistency. It does not address the per-superblock slab cache creation/destruction, cache naming, or remount name-collision issue described in the root cause.

The change only moves xattr cache initialization earlier and adds cleanup on registration failure. It does not address the core bug of per-superblock slab cache name collisions caused by cache reuse/merging across remounts.

candidates.rationale: This creates a per-superblock slab cache name derived from the device number, which is the core cause of the remount name collision when the cache is destroyed and recreated while shared slab objects may still exist.
This is the per-superblock cache creation itself; recreating a cache with the same device-based name on remount triggers the slab name collision problem described in the root cause.

Destroying the per-superblock cache during unmount allows later remounts to recreate a cache with the same name, which conflicts with slab core cache merging/lifetime behavior and leads to the warning.
This teardown in superblock cleanup is the direct action that removes the cache and makes the later remount attempt to create another identically named cache, exposing the collision bug.
This unwind-path cleanup also destroys the per-superblock xattr cache, contributing to the same destroy/recreate cycle that causes the slab name collision on subsequent mounts.

vuln_statements.explanation: This creates the per-superblock slab cache name from the device number. Recreating the cache on remount with the same derived name can collide with an existing shared slab cache object, which is the root cause.

This is the actual per-superblock xattr slab cache creation. Because the cache name is device-based and the cache may be recreated after teardown, this statement triggers the kmem_cache_create() name collision on remount.

Destroying the per-superblock cache enables the destroy/recreate cycle across mounts. With slab merging and shared cache objects, this teardown contributes directly to the remount name collision warning.
This superblock cleanup call tears down the inline xattr cache during unmount, which makes later remounts recreate the same device-named cache and exposes the collision.
